concepts.def: Who actually pays a tax — buyer or seller.
Inelastic goods bear most tax on consumer.
Tax on cigarettes, alcohol to deter use.
Demand more elastic in long run.
% change in demand for X ÷ % change in price of Y.

walkthroughs.body_html: When demand is inelastic (cigarettes), firms can pass the tax onto consumers — buyers bear most. When demand is elastic, consumers walk away, so firms swallow more of the tax. That's why governments target inelastic goods for revenue.

A train company with monopoly routes (inelastic) pushes peak fares up. A small coffee shop in a busy street (elastic — substitutes everywhere) competes by lowering price. Smart firms estimate PED before changing prices.

PED estimates aren't perfect. They change over time, vary by income level, and depend on the size of the price change. Always mention: 'However, PED may differ in the long run as consumers find substitutes.'

mcqs.q: Why do governments tax cigarettes heavily?
options: Demand is elastic, so revenue rises
Demand is inelastic, so consumers still buy and revenue is high
To make firms close down
To increase consumption

mcqs.q: Which factor makes demand MORE elastic in the long run?
options: No substitutes ever appear
Consumers find substitutes over time
The good becomes a necessity
Income falls

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: Demand always falls when supply increases.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.
A change in price shifts the demand curve.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
